An accepted worse molecule remains the source of that walk's next edit, while a separate archive preserves the best observed score. Its eight edit operators check molecular parsing, connectivity, canonical identity and novelty, but have no reference for whether a new local chemical environment occurs in ordinary molecular data.
approach.novelty: Add one frozen local chemistry support gate to the existing edit proposals. A small vocabulary extracted from unlabeled corpus molecules will identify supported atom environments; a proposed neighbor must not introduce or multiply an unsupported environment relative to its generating state. This addresses the observed drift into unusual ring atoms and bonds while allowing existing unusual environments to remain or disappear. This lineage has only its root, so no sibling has tested a corpus-derived support gate. The experiment asks whether restricting local chemical changes makes the same annealed walks more productive.

hypothesis: Condition the Parent's existing graph-edit proposal distribution on a frozen unlabeled-corpus vocabulary of local atom environments, rejecting an otherwise valid novel neighbor whenever it introduces or increases the multiplicity of an unsupported environment relative to that walk's scored source state.

finding_summary.headline: New unsupported environments fell to zero; the one-seed mean score rose from 0.233 to 0.268
finding_summary.insights:
The parent really was entering local environments absent or rare in the corpus: roughly one proposal in five increased their multiplicity. Supported alternatives were available with little extra retry work, so that behavior was avoidable without changing annealing or sacrificing evaluation budget. The same-run rejection traces establish this intermediate effect directly; the mixed score response leaves open whether removing these environments is broadly useful or primarily changes which stochastic paths are reached. The gain exceeds the declared 0.002 mean-score target on this seed, but one improving objective and one declining objective do not show a universal advantage or isolate which blocked chemistry caused either change.

Complete local support still allowed the chemistry assessment to find hydroperoxides, peracids, crowded bridges and N-Cl bonds. The N-Cl center environment itself occurred in eight sampled corpus molecules, so its survival follows the declared threshold rather than exposing a bypass. The improved drd2_docking maximum also retains a hydroperoxide and crowded ring topology. Local empirical support therefore narrows chemical drift but does not certify whole-molecule geometry, stability or synthetic plausibility. Coherent ring and functional-group changes remain worth investigating with rules shared across objectives. All starting and working child molecules were locally supported here, so preservation or removal of inherited unsupported environments remains an untested use case.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism happened on all five objectives. Using the same frozen vocabulary for both runs, 298 of 1,450 parent proposals introduced or multiplied an unsupported atom environment (20.55%); none of the 1,450 child proposals did. The mean number of introduced unsupported environments fell from 0.311 per proposal to exactly zero. The gate rejected 235 otherwise valid novel candidates and redirected 205 proposal requests to supported alternatives from the same unchanged scored source. All batches remained full, and attempts per emitted molecule rose modestly from 1.165 to 1.364. Every Metropolis decision, cooling value, working-state update and archive check agreed with the inherited rules.

On the sole evaluated seed, the mean of the five best scores rose from 0.233114 to 0.268497 (+0.035383). The improvement came from drd2_docking, which rose from 0.044776 to 0.280588. Zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.381715 to 0.322816; deco_hop stayed at 0.557517, median_2 at 0.167839, and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.013725. All 1,450 child proposals were evaluated without invalid or duplicate entries. These are single-seed results and do not establish repeatability.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families remain, but many descendants accumulate peroxide groups, crowded bridges and poorly controlled functional-group changes.
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-39a65c2978c0 against Parent n-6a8d103b076c uses the supplied digest and complete saved seed-0 trajectories for all five tasks; no task is missing. Each task contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output spans small branched alkyl halides, indole carboxamides, polyaryl chromone-like structures, fused nitrogenous diones, cyclic thiones, sugar-like acetals and heavily edited polycycles. This is considerable ring chemistry, with moderate diversity across recognizable starting families and their descendants. The digest ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 on every task, whereas aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.6655 to 0.7138. These are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 59.1 to 61.5 characters; they indicate string size, not molecular weight. All charged_rate and stereocentre_rate readings are 0.0: potentially protonatable nitrogens and stereogenic structures still occur, but their charge and stereochemistry are not explicitly specified. Relative to the Parent, phosphorus disappears from the full proposed-SMILES sets, and aromatic-bearing strings become more frequent on every task. The remaining chemistry still includes hydroperoxides, peracids, N-O substituents, occasional N-Cl bonds, highly connected small rings and crowded aminal/acetal systems. Ordinary early indole and dione structures are more readily recognizable as synthetic targets than many late cages. The latter warrant scrutiny for geometric feasibility, stability and synthesis; SMILES alone does not establish that they are impossible or establish a synthetic route. Per-task comparisons below describe the reported scores without assigning pharmacological meaning. Digest medians written as 0.0 are rounded summaries, not evidence that all those scores were exactly zero.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional upper-end molecule is an ethoxy/methoxy/phenol-substituted indole bearing a fluorophenyl carboxamide. Related upper-end structures retain the indole NH and amide but acquire N-O substitution and extra ring connections. A second upper-end family consists of cyclic thioureas attached to contracted, partly unsaturated carbocycles; some no longer have ordinary aromatic rings. The low end contains much larger branched amide/urea/acid-rich structures and crowded oxygen/nitrogen/sulfur polycycles. Mean SMILES length is 59.5 characters, and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6655. The early indole carboxamide looks synthetically plausible in outline; the later contracted-ring and cage structures are substantially more questionable.
liabilities: Upper-end cyclic thiourea derivatives include highly compressed unsaturated ring systems; evaluation 293 even contains a four-membered diene ring. Their geometry and accessibility need chemical scrutiny.
Low evaluations 262 and 272 carry N-Cl bonds on carbonyl-bound nitrogen. Other low or final molecules carry hydroperoxides and crowded aminal/acetal networks.
Many late structures combine extensive branching, several polar functionalities and unspecified stereochemistry, making the synthetic target less well defined than the early indole.
missing_features: The low-scoring bulk lacks the compact, organized indole/aryl-carbonyl arrangement present in the leading examples; many descendants replace it with large nonaromatic polar frameworks.

The excerpts do not show a sustained series of simpler, synthetically coherent alternatives that retain the favorable phenol/ether/carboxamide arrangement while varying it independently of ring contraction or N-O insertion. The scores do not identify a specific absent target group.

The much larger urea/acid-rich evaluation 252 scores 2.9203128686642823e-43; the reported median rounds to 0.0. Evaluation 296 contains a peroxy ester linkage in a ring, and evaluation 297 contains a peroxide substituent. Their scores do not certify ordinary compound stability.

The leading indole includes an N-O linkage and a methoxymethylamino substituent; these are real functional groups, but their compatibility and stability require attention rather than an assumption that an aromatic scaffold makes every decoration benign.
missing_features: The low-scoring tail lacks the extended aromatic surfaces and organized polar substitution visible in the upper-end indoles and polyaryl carbonyl compounds.

The upper-end sample lacks a clearly established simpler series that separates the contribution of those substituents from extra bridge formation. No particular unobserved scaffold or decoration can be deduced from this narrow observed score span.

A less extensively fused hydroxylated polyaryl chromone at evaluation 48 scores 0.5515878333110009, while the densely bridged nitrile-bearing evaluation 298 scores 0.5553918460218583. Both sit above the small nonaromatic evaluations 91 and 201 at 0.5. This supports an association with decorated aromatic surfaces and heteroatom/carbonyl substitution in this sample. It does not show that complicated ring fusion is required: the chemically different aromatic examples occupy a close score band. The median is 0.524481, and the late peroxidic evaluation 296 still receives 0.5435671594841145.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-end family is a large, densely connected aza-aromatic/aryl-ether polycycle carrying amino groups, non-amide ring nitrogens, an N-methyl unsaturated amine ring and a hydroperoxymethyl substituent. A distinct upper-end example is an aminated aryl/cyclic-thiourea structure with a substituted cyclohexene. The low end includes small nonaromatic oxygen heterocycles and aldehydes, but also the chemically conventional initial quinoline/phenoxy amide with N-methylpiperidine and hydroxamate. Mean SMILES length is 61.5 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6897, compared with the Parent trajectory value 0.5172. The leading cages are questionable synthetic targets despite their familiar component groups.
liabilities: The leading evaluation 266 and close analogues retain a hydroperoxymethyl group and an aryl O-N linkage. Their positive score association is not evidence of biological stability or a useful peroxide mechanism.
Extensive bridges and aminal-like connections make conformational feasibility and synthesis uncertain; no explicit stereochemistry resolves the resulting possible configurations.
The initial conventional scaffold scores poorly, while highly unusual descendants score better, so synthetic plausibility cannot be inferred from the score alone.
missing_features: The leading family does not demonstrate a peroxide-free, less crowded presentation of its aromatic surface and non-amide ring amines with comparable reported scores; the stable alternatives needed to disentangle those features are not shown.

Basic centres and fused aromatics are already present. What is poorly represented at the upper end is a range of independently varied, synthetically coherent linker and ring arrangements that separates nitrogen placement from cage formation. The trajectories do not establish a missing receptor-specific group.

The local gradient therefore depends on nitrogen placement, substitution and shape, not simply nitrogen abundance. Evaluation 251, a small fluorinated oxygen heterocycle with aldehyde, scores 0.001385268283468699. Initial evaluation 6 already contains an ordinary N-methylpiperidine attached through a phenoxy-amide/quinoline framework and scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so a basic ring amine is not an absent feature or a sufficient explanation. per_task.generated_character: The leading observed structure is the initial ethyl hydroxybenzoate bearing a phenyl-substituted, N-methylated fused nitrogenous dione. The strongest proposed descendants keep much of that framework, or belong to the quinoline/phenoxy/N-methylpiperidine family bearing a hydroxamate or peracid. Low scorers are small branched bromochloroalkanes and an alcohol; late examples become mixed aromatic/nonaromatic polycycles with thioesters, peroxides, amines and sulfonamides. Mean SMILES length is 59.1 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7. The intact early aromatic dione and amide frameworks are plausible synthetic targets in outline; the peracid-bearing and highly bridged descendants are less persuasive.
liabilities: Peracids replace hydroxamates in several near-leading descendants, and evaluation 296 retains a carbonyl-O-OH group in a crowded nitrogenous cage. These are potentially reactive functionalities even when the scalar score is unchanged.
Ring contraction and arbitrary connections progressively erode the recognizable initial scaffold without an observed improvement over its score.
The small alkyl-halide tail offers little organized aromatic/polar architecture; later cages supply many connections but unspecified stereochemistry.
missing_features: The lower-end molecules lack the extended aryl/heteroaryl and organized carbonyl architecture of the leading starting structure.

The proposed upper end does not demonstrate a coherent alternative arrangement that improves on the initial aromatic dione while preserving ordinary functional-group chemistry. The trajectories alone cannot specify an unseen similarity target or a particular missing fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329 and remains the maximum in both Child and Parent. Replacing its pendant phenyl with a nonaromatic cyclopentadiene gives the best proposed evaluation 27 at 0.15882451078226317; adding a phenolic substituent to the pendant phenyl gives evaluation 17 at 0.15625847779496568. The bromochlorinated low examples at evaluations 31 and 101 both score 0.015094447095057544. In the other upper-end family, replacing the hydroxamate at evaluation 26 with a peracid at evaluation 36 leaves the reported score exactly 0.1506011755487833. per_task.generated_character: The leading molecule is an ethyl ester on a phenolic, ring-connected aryl/fused-nitrogenous-dione framework; its ester is not a lactone. Another relatively high family consists of much smaller fluorinated, hydroxylated carbocycles bearing methylthio carbinol groups. An indole-amide-derived family also appears but is strongly bridged and N-O substituted. The deepest low end consists of large branched nonaromatic amide/urea/acid frameworks with numerous amines; final molecules include crowded sulfur/oxygen/nitrogen polycycles and hydroperoxides. Mean SMILES length is 61.3 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6931, compared with 0.5 in the Parent. Fluorinated aliphatic chemistry is present in a relatively high example. What is not demonstrated is a coherent, synthetically comfortable series combining controlled polar-group placement and tractable ring geometry. These very low and heterogeneous scores do not identify a specific absent pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes a four-membered diene-containing cyclic-thiourea derivative, densely bridged aromatic lactone-like structures and high-scoring aza-aromatic aminal cages. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 throughout, yet recognizable early aromatic scaffolds often become crowded polycycles. Removing phosphorus from the output has not removed these whole-structure concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve tractable whole-molecule ring geometry when it creates new connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposal construction needs a task-independent way to account for complete ring size, bridge connectivity and geometric feasibility. Transformations that preserve or replace coherent ring units could provide useful chemical variation without continuously adding difficult connections; local atom-environment familiarity alone cannot establish global synthetic plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited hydroxamate-to-peracid pair has identical reported score 0.1506011755487833. The leading aza-aromatic amine family retains a hydroperoxymethyl substituent, and low-scoring amide-rich examples contain N-Cl bonds. N-O groups also occur among both ordinary-looking and highly modified structures; their presence is not proof that the entire molecule is unusable.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group variation does not consistently distinguish stable candidate chemistry from potentially reactive peroxide and N-halogen motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic transformation repertoire should treat intact functional groups and their compatibility explicitly, and make stable alternatives accessible without requiring unrelated scaffold distortion. Peroxide and N-halogen chemistry needs a deliberate policy based on chemical evidence; favorable scalar feedback alone does not establish stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper end includes a recognizable phenolic indole carboxamide and an initial aromatic fused dione that no proposed molecule surpasses in its own trajectory. Several low-end families instead become large nonaromatic amino/acid-rich structures. Aromatic-bearing string rates of 0.6655 to 0.7138 coexist with a ring-closure rate of 0.9655, so rings are abundant while recognizable aromatic organization is less consistently retained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks a consistently demonstrated route to vary useful aromatic and carbonyl arrangements without accumulating unrelated structural changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include chemically coherent scaffold-preserving substitutions, ring-unit replacements and simplifying edits that vary donor/acceptor placement or linker geometry independently. These capabilities should use current objective-local feedback to discover where they help, without encoding a preferred benchmark scaffold or hidden objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the cited molecules include substituted small rings, bridged aminals and crowded acetals. This is absence of stereochemical SMILES annotation, not evidence that the molecules lack stereocentres. Charged_rate is also 0.0 despite non-amide amine groups, so neutral text should not be confused with absence of ionizable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted polycyclic chemistry does not specify stereochemical identity despite creating potentially stereogenic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and represent newly created stereogenic structures deliberately when constructing candidates. Comparisons among well-defined configurations would make these chemical proposals more interpretable; the current trajectories do not establish whether that representation change would improve a scalar score.

method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

applicability_conditions: The chemical support vocabulary must be built solely from the permitted unlabeled corpus before objective feedback and must remain identical across independent objective processes. All scores and persistent walk states remain local to the current objective.

The intervention is useful only if the Parent frequently introduces local environments below the frozen corpus support threshold and those changes are less productive than available supported alternatives. This is a testable extrapolation from the Parent's molecular assessment, not a conclusion already established by it.

The comparison tolerates unsupported environments inherited from supplied initial molecules or earlier working states only without increasing each unsupported signature's multiplicity. The gate can remove such environments, but it is not a mechanism for replacing the initial scaffold or restarting from a better molecule.

Radius-one environment support describes local empirical chemistry. It does not certify synthesis, molecular stability, global ring strain, pharmacology or objective relevance, and it can exclude rare but useful chemical changes. Those limits remain even if activation is exact.

Enough supported novel neighbors must remain within the Parent's bounded retry loop to preserve full batches. Severe rejection or loss of useful structural transitions can make this gate detrimental despite improved local support.

The supplied Curate cluster history is empty, and the examined campaign observations contain no previous attempt at this local-environment support-gate mechanism. The lineage has only its Parent root, so no settled sibling result is being revisited.

The available Parent score and chemical assessment come from one screening replica. They motivate this experiment but do not establish a multi-seed effect or justify altering the protocol-supplied evaluation settings.

research_intent.falsifier: The support-gate mechanism is refuted if any emitted proposal has D>0 under the published frozen signature table, a rejected proposal with D=0 was rejected by an undeclared chemistry rule, a positive-D candidate passes through a fallback, or the alleged supported replacement was produced by changing the scored walk source before real feedback. A changed vocabulary across objectives, corpus-molecule retrieval, task-specific chemical rules, or changes to Metropolis acceptance, cooling or archive behavior violate the bound experiment. Complete traces with no otherwise eligible positive-D candidates rejected and redirected leave the mechanism unactivated; they do not establish success merely because emitted violations are zero. If the Parent's retrospective positive-D rate is zero, the claimed Parent bottleneck is not supported by this signature definition. Missing per-attempt evidence or an unreproducible table makes activation inconclusive. Exhausting the retained attempt bound or failing a full valid novel batch refutes generative viability. If the gate redirects proposals and eliminates new unsupported environments while scores fail to improve, that is negative score evidence for the activated mechanism, not a falsification of its execution.
research_intent.implementation_change: Change only optimize.py to add this support gate and the preparation and diagnostics required by it. During the existing prepare command, use the supplied preparation RNG seed to reservoir-sample at most 100,000 nonempty records from the supplied unlabeled corpus, parse and canonicalize them, and count each atom-environment signature at most once per distinct sampled canonical molecule. Skip invalid records. A signature is the center tuple (atomic number, formal charge, aromatic flag, radical-electron count, heavy-atom degree, total attached hydrogens) paired with the sorted multiset of (neighbor atomic number, neighbor formal charge, neighbor aromatic flag, connecting bond order) for all heavy-atom neighbors. Compute signatures after sanitization and canonical-SMILES reparsing with identical code in preparation and runtime; encode aromatic bond order consistently as 1.5. A signature is supported exactly when it occurs in at least five distinct sampled molecules. Publish only the signature-count table, its schema and support threshold, sampling configuration and aggregate preparation receipts with the existing annealing configuration; retain no corpus molecule strings, molecular candidate library, labels or task-conditioned artifact. At runtime load this immutable table. molecular_assessment.overall_character: Assessment of n-39a65c2978c0 against Parent n-6a8d103b076c uses the supplied digest and complete saved seed-0 trajectories for all five tasks; no task is missing. Each task contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output spans small branched alkyl halides, indole carboxamides, polyaryl chromone-like structures, fused nitrogenous diones, cyclic thiones, sugar-like acetals and heavily edited polycycles. This is considerable ring chemistry, with moderate diversity across recognizable starting families and their descendants. The digest ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 on every task, whereas aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.6655 to 0.7138. These are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 59.1 to 61.5 characters; they indicate string size, not molecular weight. All charged_rate and stereocentre_rate readings are 0.0: potentially protonatable nitrogens and stereogenic structures still occur, but their charge and stereochemistry are not explicitly specified. Relative to the Parent, phosphorus disappears from the full proposed-SMILES sets, and aromatic-bearing strings become more frequent on every task. The remaining chemistry still includes hydroperoxides, peracids, N-O substituents, occasional N-Cl bonds, highly connected small rings and crowded aminal/acetal systems. Ordinary early indole and dione structures are more readily recognizable as synthetic targets than many late cages. The latter warrant scrutiny for geometric feasibility, stability and synthesis; SMILES alone does not establish that they are impossible or establish a synthetic route. Per-task comparisons below describe the reported scores without assigning pharmacological meaning. Digest medians written as 0.0 are rounded summaries, not evidence that all those scores were exactly zero.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional upper-end molecule is an ethoxy/methoxy/phenol-substituted indole bearing a fluorophenyl carboxamide. Related upper-end structures retain the indole NH and amide but acquire N-O substitution and extra ring connections. A second upper-end family consists of cyclic thioureas attached to contracted, partly unsaturated carbocycles; some no longer have ordinary aromatic rings. The low end contains much larger branched amide/urea/acid-rich structures and crowded oxygen/nitrogen/sulfur polycycles. Mean SMILES length is 59.5 characters, and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6655. The early indole carboxamide looks synthetically plausible in outline; the later contracted-ring and cage structures are substantially more questionable.
liabilities: Upper-end cyclic thiourea derivatives include highly compressed unsaturated ring systems; evaluation 293 even contains a four-membered diene ring. Their geometry and accessibility need chemical scrutiny.
Low evaluations 262 and 272 carry N-Cl bonds on carbonyl-bound nitrogen. Other low or final molecules carry hydroperoxides and crowded aminal/acetal networks.
Many late structures combine extensive branching, several polar functionalities and unspecified stereochemistry, making the synthetic target less well defined than the early indole.
missing_features: The low-scoring bulk lacks the compact, organized indole/aryl-carbonyl arrangement present in the leading examples; many descendants replace it with large nonaromatic polar frameworks.

The excerpts do not show a sustained series of simpler, synthetically coherent alternatives that retain the favorable phenol/ether/carboxamide arrangement while varying it independently of ring contraction or N-O insertion. The scores do not identify a specific absent target group.

applicability_conditions: The chemical support vocabulary must be built solely from the permitted unlabeled corpus before objective feedback and must remain identical across independent objective processes. All scores and persistent walk states remain local to the current objective.

The intervention is useful only if the Parent frequently introduces local environments below the frozen corpus support threshold and those changes are less productive than available supported alternatives. This is a testable extrapolation from the Parent's molecular assessment, not a conclusion already established by it.

The comparison tolerates unsupported environments inherited from supplied initial molecules or earlier working states only without increasing each unsupported signature's multiplicity. The gate can remove such environments, but it is not a mechanism for replacing the initial scaffold or restarting from a better molecule.

Radius-one environment support describes local empirical chemistry. It does not certify synthesis, molecular stability, global ring strain, pharmacology or objective relevance, and it can exclude rare but useful chemical changes. Those limits remain even if activation is exact.

Enough supported novel neighbors must remain within the Parent's bounded retry loop to preserve full batches. Severe rejection or loss of useful structural transitions can make this gate detrimental despite improved local support.

The supplied Curate cluster history is empty, and the examined campaign observations contain no previous attempt at this local-environment support-gate mechanism. The lineage has only its Parent root, so no settled sibling result is being revisited.

The available Parent score and chemical assessment come from one screening replica. They motivate this experiment but do not establish a multi-seed effect or justify altering the protocol-supplied evaluation settings.

approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps independent molecular graph walks, each starting from a supplied scored molecule. It proposes random atom or bond edits from each current state, evaluates one neighbor per scheduled walk, accepts improvements, and sometimes accepts a loss using a temperature that falls as feedback arrives. An accepted worse molecule remains the source of that walk's next edit, while a separate archive preserves the best observed score. Its eight edit operators check molecular parsing, connectivity, canonical identity and novelty, but have no reference for whether a new local chemical environment occurs in ordinary molecular data.
approach.novelty: Add one frozen local chemistry support gate to the existing edit proposals. A small vocabulary extracted from unlabeled corpus molecules will identify supported atom environments; a proposed neighbor must not introduce or multiply an unsupported environment relative to its generating state. This addresses the observed drift into unusual ring atoms and bonds while allowing existing unusual environments to remain or disappear. This lineage has only its root, so no sibling has tested a corpus-derived support gate. The experiment asks whether restricting local chemical changes makes the same annealed walks more productive.

research_intent.falsifier: The support-gate mechanism is refuted if any emitted proposal has D>0 under the published frozen signature table, a rejected proposal with D=0 was rejected by an undeclared chemistry rule, a positive-D candidate passes through a fallback, or the alleged supported replacement was produced by changing the scored walk source before real feedback. A changed vocabulary across objectives, corpus-molecule retrieval, task-specific chemical rules, or changes to Metropolis acceptance, cooling or archive behavior violate the bound experiment. Complete traces with no otherwise eligible positive-D candidates rejected and redirected leave the mechanism unactivated; they do not establish success merely because emitted violations are zero. If the Parent's retrospective positive-D rate is zero, the claimed Parent bottleneck is not supported by this signature definition. Missing per-attempt evidence or an unreproducible table makes activation inconclusive. Exhausting the retained attempt bound or failing a full valid novel batch refutes generative viability. If the gate redirects proposals and eliminates new unsupported environments while scores fail to improve, that is negative score evidence for the activated mechanism, not a falsification of its execution.

research_intent.mechanism: Condition the Parent's existing graph-edit proposal distribution on a frozen unlabeled-corpus vocabulary of local atom environments, rejecting an otherwise valid novel neighbor whenever it introduces or increases the multiplicity of an unsupported environment relative to that walk's scored source state.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-6a8d103b076c executes annealing correctly but expends its proposal budget on an excessively permissive graph-edit neighborhood. Its available summary and run log report a macro score of 0.233114420388057, including 0.04477593818961592 on drd2_docking and 0.013725075295981876 on sitagliptin_mpo, with no improvement over initialization on median_2. These are results from the sole available screening replica; the aggregate is incomplete and its reported zero deviation does not establish reliability. The activation audit reproduces all 1,450 Metropolis decisions, verifies the cooling schedule, and confirms later reuse of 546 of 557 accepted downhill states. The molecular assessment instead identifies aromatic phosphorus, unusual phosphorus/sulfur centers and nitrogen-halogen bonds, with ordinary aromatic content in only about half to two thirds of proposals. The source shows that atom replacement and bond editing are admitted after sanitization without a learned or empirical local-chemistry constraint. The causal hypothesis is that admitting locally unsupported chemical changes contributes to unproductive walks; the existing evidence does not prove that a corpus support restriction will improve scores.
